title: Vostok and EPICA Dome C ice cores
summary: Deep Antarctic ice cores gave a continuous record of past climate and greenhouse gases. The Vostok core covered the past 420,000 years; the EPICA Dome C core, reported in Nature in 2004, reached 740,000 years, and the EPICA team later described a record back 800 000 years. Atmospheric CO2 and methane are now at their highest levels in that span.

uncertainty.note: The pin year is the oldest extent of the record, 800 000 years back, converted with year = 1950 - 800000 (assumption: the page gives no reference year). The 2004 Nature paper itself reports 740,000 years; the 420,000-year Vostok figure comes from that paper's abstract.

importance.justification: These cores are the main ice-core record of glacial cycles and greenhouse gases over about 800,000 years.
